description: Sentiment track, SG03: minimal pairs for the hard-case types found in the SR02 dev errors (Ammar, 2026-10-30, option A of the headline convention: a headline that only reports an event is neutral, for good and bad events). Each request asks for two tweets on the same subject that differ only in what sets the label. Tweet A is the target type, tweet B the contrast. The few-shot pairs are fixed per type: side A (or B for complaint/fan) is a real S1-train tweet (ids in `source_ids`, wrapping quotes trimmed), the other side was written by Claude and approved by Ammar. A random subject hint per request adds variety. Placeholders: {task} {examples} {variety_name} {variety_instruction} {hint}. Names in the hints are in Arabic script (a 24-request Qwen3 test on 2026-10-30 copied English names into the tweets).
system: You are an Arabic-speaking social media user who writes posts on Twitter.

msa.name: Modern Standard Arabic
msa.instruction: Use Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not a dialect.

egypt.name: Egyptian Arabic
egypt.instruction: Use the Egyptian dialect, not Modern Standard Arabic.

gulf.name: Gulf Arabic
gulf.instruction: Use the Gulf dialect (as spoken in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain or Oman), not Modern Standard Arabic.

levant.name: Levantine Arabic
levant.instruction: Use the Levantine dialect (as spoken in Syria, Lebanon, Jordan or Palestine), not Modern Standard Arabic.

news_bad.task:
Write a pair of tweets about the same bad-news event.
Tweet A is a news headline that only reports the event in a factual tone, the way a news account posts it. The writer adds no opinion and no feeling, so its sentiment is neutral, even though the event is bad.
Tweet B reports the same event, but the writer adds their own anger, sadness or criticism, so its sentiment is negative.

complaint.task:
Write a pair of short, informal tweets in dialect about the same everyday situation, each under 15 words.
Tweet A is a complaint: the writer is annoyed, disappointed, bored or fed up with the situation, so its sentiment is negative.
Tweet B describes the same situation in the same dialect but only as plain information or a question, with no complaint and no feeling, so its sentiment is neutral.

lyric_pos.task:
Write a pair of tweets about the same song or singer.
Tweet A only quotes one or two lines in the style of a song or poem by the given singer or poet, the way people post lyrics they are listening to, optionally followed by the name as a hashtag. Invent new lines; do not quote real lyrics. The writer adds no opinion of their own, so its sentiment is neutral, even if the lines are emotional.
Tweet B is about the same singer or poet, but in the writer's own words, praising the song or saying how much they love it, so its sentiment is positive.

lyric_neg.task:

Tweet A only quotes one or two sad lines in the style of a song or poem by the given singer or poet, the way people post lyrics they are listening to, optionally followed by the name as a hashtag. Tweet B expresses the same sad feeling as the writer's own, about their own life, in their own words and without quoting, so its sentiment is negative.

fan_post.task:
Write a pair of short tweets about the same celebrity, team, show or product.
Tweet A is a post by a fan or a fan account: it celebrates, greets, wishes luck to or shows love for them, mostly through hashtags, emojis and short phrases, so its sentiment is positive. It is not a news headline.
Tweet B is about the same celebrity, team, show or product, but only gives plain information (a time, a place, a fact), with no celebration and no praise, so its sentiment is neutral.
